sm: The speaker, Robert Marks, answers audience questions about whether AI will become self-aware. He says the question first requires defining self-aware, and notes that consciousness has many competing theories, including panpsychism and integrated information theory, which he mocks with a joke about looking for a pony in horse manure. He favors dualism, the view that the mind is greater than the brain, and points to a book he co-edited called Minding the Brain. He says mapping and copying every neuron would not recreate a person, and that uploading a brain would capture only its algorithmic part. He argues creativity shows up as flashes of genius, citing Gauss, Tesla and Paul McCartney's song Yesterday, and concludes a computer will never have one.
